title: Determine if String Halves Are Alike
statement:
The string `s` has an even length and is made of English letters in either case. Cut it in the middle into a front half and a back half of the same length. Return `true` if both halves contain the same number of vowels, and `false` otherwise.

The vowels are `a`, `e`, `i`, `o`, `u` in lowercase or uppercase; every occurrence counts, so a repeated vowel is counted each time it appears.
constraints: s contains only uppercase and lowercase English letters
notes:
## Intuition

Only one number matters per half: how many vowels it holds. Slicing the string and counting each slice works, but a single loop over the first half can count both halves at once, because position `i` in the front matches position `i + half` in the back.

## Approach

1. Put the ten vowels, lowercase and uppercase, in the set `vowels` so each check is O(1).
2. Let `half` be `s.length / 2`.
3. For each `i` from 0 to `half - 1`, add 1 to `firstCount` if `s[i]` is a vowel and add 1 to `secondCount` if `s[i + half]` is a vowel.
4. Return whether the two counts are equal.

## Example 1, step by step

`s = "book"`, so `half = 2`.

- `i = 0`: `s[0] = 'b'` is not a vowel; `s[2] = 'o'` is, so `secondCount = 1`.
- `i = 1`: `s[1] = 'o'` is a vowel, so `firstCount = 1`; `s[3] = 'k'` is not.

Both counts are 1, so the answer is `true`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): each character is checked once.
- Space: O(1): the vowel set has a fixed ten letters.

## Pitfalls

- Uppercase vowels count too; checking only `'aeiou'` fails on inputs like `"AA"`.
- `y` is not a vowel here.
- Count every vowel occurrence; a half with `"oo"` has two vowels, not one.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `vowels` | set of the ten vowel characters |
| `half` | length of each half |
| `firstCount` | vowels seen in the front half |
| `secondCount` | vowels seen in the back half |
| `i` | position in the front half; `i + half` is the matching back position |

narration.2: Store both cases of every vowel so a lookup is a single set check.
narration.3: Each half has exactly this many characters.
narration.4: Vowels found in the front half so far.
narration.5: Vowels found in the back half so far.
narration.6: Walk the front half; each step also looks at the matching back position.
narration.7: Is the front character a vowel?
narration.8: Yes: count it for the front half.
narration.10: Check the character at the same offset in the back half.
narration.11: Yes: count it for the back half.
narration.14: The halves are alike exactly when their vowel counts match.
